accuracy.evidence: Definition and spelling rule taken from the National Curriculum English Appendix 1 Year 1 statement that each part is spelt as it would be on its own, and the meaning link from CCSS L.2.4d. Head-final structure (goldfish is a fish, houseboat vs boathouse) checked against Bauer's English Word-formation and the Cambridge Grammar of the English Language, with exocentric exceptions (pickpocket) and open or hyphenated compounds noted in the adult text so the rule is not overstated. Each compound (sunshine, football, earring, cupcake, snowman, toothbrush, bedroom, playground, farmyard, blackberry, raincoat, raindrop, rainbow, rainfall, birdhouse) and each non-compound (carpet, button, season, target, bandage, rabbit) was checked in the Oxford and Cambridge dictionaries; carpet, button and season come from single Old French or Latin roots, not two English words.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the spelling and reading slips teachers report for KS1 compounds: dropping the doubled letter at the join (earring in the step 1 prediction, p3 and the challenge), splitting at the wrong place (step 2 feedback names which part is not a word, challenge 'cut'), treating any long word with a little word inside as a compound (carpet, button, season in step 4, p5, m9 and the challenge), reversing the parts (houseboat or boathouse in step 3, m2, m6) and inventing non-words (rainsit, rainpen in step 5 and m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcmpd works on whole-word morphemes: gluing two free words, cutting at the morpheme boundary, ordering by the head word and rejecting false compounds. flagsyl claps beats inside words and flagrime builds words from onset and rime, so neither has word-plus-word joins, head-word order or hidden-word tricks; flagrhyme judges end sounds. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by doing: shine dropped in the first box is turned back with 'shinesun is not a word', earring appears in two colours showing both r's kept, a wrong cut in toothbrush is marked in red with which part is not a word, house first gives the wrong thing for the clue, carpet bounces out of the compound box with the reason, and rainsit is rejected as not a real word. The text after each task only confirms what the child just saw.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'earing' (many children write it; the glue step shows both r's), 'Yes, they use the same two words' for houseboat and boathouse (the order step gives two different things), and 'Yes, it has two words in it' for carpet (the sort step rejects it).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions; every wrong option is tagged with one of nine distinct messages naming the slip: hidden words are not a compound, a part that is not a word (sunny), a dropped letter, a gap in a closed compound, a wrong cut, the wrong order, two things not one, a made-up non-word, and long is not compound.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words, with examples in every paragraph, and pass the family kid readability limit; the adult text names the Year 1 appendix wording, CCSS L.2.4d and the terms compound word, root word, morpheme, closed compound and head word. Canvas text is short labels; every word tile is spoken on tap where speech is available, and the young layout gives big tiles and buttons.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (what a compound is, keep every letter, find the two words to read it, the last word gives the meaning and false compounds). Items cover splitting (p1, p4, m7), spelling at the join (p3, m3), false compounds (p5, m1, m9), head word meaning (m2, m6), real versus made-up (m5), the definition (m8) and counting (p2, m4).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and 360 px screenshots of every step before and after Show me: the two glue boxes, plus, equals and picture fit in one row; six word tiles sit in a 3 by 2 grid with readable words; the 10 letters of toothbrush fit at about 33 px a letter with the cut found from the nearest gap; the sort card and two bins fit with sorted words listed inside; the six rain petals ring the centre without overlap. Mouse drags into the glue boxes and the sort bins complete the tasks.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: add each word, every possible cut of the current word, put a word first or last, sort the current card into either box, and try each rain ending. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with why the move worked or not. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
